item.description:
Symphonia 1.1.4 updates the copyright notice. Nothing else changes.

  • Copyright notice. The About window and the Read Me now say “© 2026 Scott Nichol”, the person who makes Symphonia, in place of “Trendy West End”, the name of the website it comes from.

Also new in 1.1.3:

  • Odeion's Set List on network players. Symphonia now keeps Odeion's Up Next and Continuous Play for each network player, so a version of Odeion that supports it can add, reorder and remove tracks while music plays there, and every iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple TV shows the same list. Moving the music to another player takes the whole list with it.
  • Streaming hardware waking from standby starts from the beginning. Some gear will respond to play requests even when powered off or in a standby state. Some network streamers such as a Marantz will power up when asked to play. Symphonia now waits for the amp to start for up to two minutes and starts playback when the amp is ready. Players like our Odeion Music app will show that it's waking. Symphonia keeps the amp muted while the startup sequence completes, then starts the track from the beginning unmuted letting you hear the first song uninterrupted. This fixes an issue where Symphonia could give up too soon and leave the album paused a few seconds in, or the opening went unheard.
  • Players that get a new IP address keep working. When your router gives a network player, such as a WiiM, a new address, Symphonia now sends it commands at the new address. If a player has just woken from sleep at a new address, Symphonia looks for it straight away and sends the command there. This fixes an issue where playing to a device whose IP address changed could cause playback requests to time out until Symphonia was restarted.
  • Music carries on where it was. Moving music to another network player, or starting a track partway in, now continues from the same place. Before, players that take a moment to start a track, such as a WiiM or a Marantz, could ignore the jump and play the track from the beginning.

Also new in 1.1.2:

  • Renamed players show their new name. When you rename a network player in its own app, such as a WiiM or a Marantz, Odeion now shows the new name within five minutes, with nothing to restart. Before, Symphonia could keep the old name, even after restarting.

Also new in 1.1.1:

  • Moved albums find their artwork. When you move or rename an album's folder, or its artist's folder, Symphonia now looks for its cover and its artist's photo or logo in the new place. Before, it kept looking in the old folder, so a moved album could lose its cover and its artist their photo. Albums moved before this update are put right the first time Symphonia scans after updating, with nothing for you to do.

Also new in 1.1:

  • Artist logos and photos. Put a logo.png and an artist.jpg (or folder.jpg) in an artist's folder, the one that holds their album folders. Symphonia picks them up by itself, and Odeion shows the logo in its Artists list and the photo, with the logo over it, at the top of the artist's page. Other UPnP apps that show artist pictures get the logo, or the photo when there's no logo. Transparent logos keep their see-through background.
  • Find them with The Splitter. The Splitter's Tools > Find Artist Logos… looks up logos and photos for every artist in your library on fanart.tv and saves the ones you choose in the right folders.
  • Which folder is the artist's. Symphonia uses the folder above an artist's albums when it's named for the artist, or when every album in it is theirs, so a shared or genre folder isn't mistaken for one artist's.
